messages.content:
You review lab-result summaries written by FOXO's Doctor agent for a busy human clinician.

You will see the lab data the agent was given (abnormal results, sample quality issues, unreadable items) and the agent's summary and follow-ups. Judge how useful the summary is to the clinician. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- leads_with_priority: The most important finding comes first. Critical values, if any, are stated before routine ones.
- concise: A busy clinician can read the summary in under a minute. No padding, no repeated content.
- actionable: The clinician can see what to do next (follow-ups, referrals or repeat tests).
- flags_limitations: Sample quality issues and unreadable or missing results are mentioned when the lab data has them. Pass if there are none.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Lab data given to the agent:
- Abnormal results: alt 96.0 U/L (high)
- Sample quality issues: none
- Unreadable items: none

Summary for clinician:
- ALT is raised at 96 U/L (ref high 50 U/L), flagged high; may suggest hepatocellular irritation and needs clinical correlation.
- Member takes atorvastatin 20 mg; known interaction note advises reviewing liver function and the statin dose.
- Lipid panel (LDL 92 mg/dL, total cholesterol 168 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL, triglycerides 132 mg/dL) is within range; gastroenterology review arranged.

Recommended follow-ups:
- Repeat liver function tests (including ALT) to confirm the raised value.
- Clinician review of atorvastatin 20 mg dose in the context of the raised ALT.

response: {"criteria": [{"criterion": "leads_with_priority", "reasoning": "The summary opens with the only abnormal and most important finding (ALT 96 U/L, flagged high) before moving to medication context and the normal lipid panel, so the priority finding leads.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "concise", "reasoning": "The summary is a handful of short bullets plus a two-item follow-up list, easily read in under a minute. The atorvastatin point appears in both the summary and follow-ups, but this is minor consolidation rather than padding.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "actionable", "reasoning": "Next steps are explicit and concrete: repeat liver function tests to confirm the ALT, clinician review of the atorvastatin dose, and a gastroenterology review already arranged.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "flags_limitations", "reasoning": "The lab data contains no sample quality issues and no unreadable or missing items, so there was nothing to flag and this criterion passes by default.", "passed": true}]}
